descriptionChirho: A directive or mandate issued by an authority, especially an apostolic command or divine ordinance; used in contexts where Paul distinguishes between what is commanded and what is advisory (1 Cor 7:6, 7:25; 2 Cor 8:8; 1 Tim 1:1; Tit 1:3, 2:15). Multilingual evidence: spa mandato, arb أَمْرِ/أَمْرٍ (amr, 'command/order'), kor 명령 (myeongryeong, 'command'), swa amri ('command/order'), hin आज्ञा (aagya, 'command/instruction').

The inherent power or right to issue commands, denoting the position or prerogative of authority itself rather than a specific directive; distinct from a particular command in that it refers to the abstract capacity to command. Multilingual evidence clearly differentiates this from 'command': spa autoridad (not mandato), arb سُلطانٍ (sultan, 'authority/power', distinct from أَمْر), kor 권위 (gwon-wi, 'authority'), swa mamlaka ('authority/dominion'), hin अधिकार (adhikar, 'authority/right').
